title: A year of alloy discovery in an automated lab: a simulated benchmark (digital twin)
description:
A simulated benchmark, not lab results: two alloy-discovery campaigns replayed for a whole year in a digital twin of BYU's Vertical Cloud Lab design (PR 318), against the same campaigns run the conventional way (partner facilities and core facilities).

FLAIME searches aluminium alloys for laser powder bed fusion and ONR copper alloys for blown-powder DED. Both share one lab, one atomizer and one calendar. The video shows the two function networks, the figures we track, the year at increasing speed (one alloy start to finish on day 1, then the station cameras, then the whole lab with each station lit by the event log), and the results.

In this simulated benchmark (vertical lab + bofn_blend vs conventional + bofn):
- FLAIME (Al alloys for laser powder bed fusion): reached the state-of-the-art target 1.9x faster. Its cost against the conventional lab's: operating, no capex 136%; full, with capex 200%; operating, lab shared with outside users 84%; full, lab shared with outside users 114%.
- ONR (Cu alloys for blown-powder DED): reached the state-of-the-art target 3.7x faster. Its cost against the conventional lab's: operating, no capex 84%; full, with capex 115%; operating, lab shared with outside users 42%; full, lab shared with outside users 48%.
Against the conventional lab run with a metallurgist's heuristic instead: FLAIME 1.1x, ONR 2.2x faster to the same target; there the automated lab costs more unless outside users share it (notes/twin_econ.md).
Where BOFN doesn't win: on copper, tiered CALPHAD screening finished ahead of BOFN with blend screening (0.69 against 0.67; with a hidden gamma-2 corrosion effect, 0.69 against 0.55); on aluminium a metallurgist's heuristic reaches the state of the art sooner, and BOFN's lead is in the final alloy.

Real: the lab design's 3-D renders, the atomizer footage, the search spaces (the proposals), USGS prices and the economics' sources. Assumed: station times, fees and outside-facility delays. Simulated: the alloys' properties, every measurement and every result.

Code: https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/tree/73b155f/vertical-lab/twin (video: twin/video, write-up notes/twin_video.md)
PR: https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/pull/318
